title_original: Bifa unveils craft winners in 10 categories for 2026 awards

blocks.text: Source: Moonspun Films
‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’
Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning leads the winners of the British Independent Film Awards’ craft prizes with three awards.

The film’s prizes include Shaheen Baig for best casting – her second such award, having won for Blue Jean in 2022 – with Maya Maffioli receiving best editing and Connie Farr winning her third best music supervision Bifa, having previously won for Barnard’s Ali & Ava in 2021 and All Of Us Strangers in 2023.

blocks.text: The film won in three of the four craft categories in which it was nominated. It has four further nominations at the December ceremony, including for best British independent film.
Peter Glanz’s 18 th -century comedy-drama Savage House was the other multiple craft winner with two prizes: best make-up and hair design for Jacquetta Levon, and best costume design for Alex Bovaird.

Five films took one award each: A Long Winter (best cinematography for Andre Turpin), Ink (best production design for Gareth Pugh and Carson McColl), Rose Of Nevada (best sound for Ian Wilson and Mark Jenkin), Everybody Digs Bill Evans (best original music for Roger Goula) and The Magic Faraway Tree (best effects for Ruslan Borysov, Richard Cheal and Tim Ledbury).
The winners in all remaining categories , including best British independent film, will be announced at the Bifa ceremony at London’s Camden Roundhouse on Sunday, December 6.
Bifa 2026 craft winners
Best casting – Shaheen Baig, I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning
Best cinematography – Andre Turpin, A Long Winter
Best costume design – Alex Bovaird, Savage House
Best editing – Maya Maffioli, I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning
Best effects – Ruslan Borysov, Richard Cheal, Tim Ledbury, The Magic Faraway Tree
Best music supervision – Connie Farr, I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning
Best make-up and hair design – Jacquetta Levon, Savage House
Best original music – Roger Goula, Everybody Digs Bill Evans
Best production design – Gareth Pugh, Carson McColl, Ink
Best sound – Mark Jenkin, Ian Wilson, Rose Of Nevada
